description: Estimated historical language presence from calibrated lineage cuts, historical periods, geographic interpolation and explicit continuity priors. Model regions overlap and are not exclusive borders. Envelopes are heuristic sensitivity regions, not calibrated probabilities.
assumptions: Uncalibrated family diversification uses a 4000 BCE weak prior and branching depth; this is a modeling assumption, not a dated linguistic result.

Unlocated ancestors use a regional core of descendant coordinates near the inherited homeland anchor, represented by a member coordinate rather than an oceanic mean. The core radius is 1800 km; curated homeland anchors and study locations take precedence.

Locations between anchors use shortest-longitude interpolation on land within 2000 km. Longer gaps and interpolated water positions use the destination anchor as a continuity prior, rather than inventing intercontinental occupancy. Actual source island points remain usable when the coarse land mask omits their islands. These distributions are not documented migration routes.
Unanchored single-year historical records receive a 700-year modeling window; named historical-stage calibrations override this fallback.
Uncertainty envelopes widen by 0.12 km per year away from an anchor, including the inherited calibration's temporal uncertainty. Their size expresses model sensitivity, not a posterior probability.
Mapped modern components distant from a language's reference location expand from an explicit expansion date, or remain restricted to the reference vicinity before the recent extrapolation period.
Historical stages and registers may overlap. Written or learned continuation does not imply continued use as a population's first language.
The model excludes pseudo-family groupings from inferred ancestry; their source records remain in the catalogue and reference map.

Lexifier/contact groupings use destination geography and approximate authored contact onsets, rather than interpolated ancestral homelands. These dates describe modeling scenarios, not precise language births.

atlas-priors.citation: Atlas authored historical scenarios: approximate contact onsets, regional continuity and spatial assumptions; not dates measured by Glottolog.

pitcairn.citation: Government of Pitcairn Islands, History: settlement in January 1790 supplies a lower bound for the modeled local contact tradition, not a precise language birth.

australian-settlement.citation: National Museum of Australia, Convict cargo: First Fleet settlement in January 1788. Atlas uses this as an Australian English expansion anchor, not a measured language boundary.

chang2015.citation: Chang et al. (2015), Language 91:194–244. Tables 7–9 and ancestry-constrained chronologies.

sagart2019.citation: Sagart et al. (2019). Dated language phylogenies shed light on the ancestry of Sino-Tibetan. PNAS 116:10317–10322. Approximate north-China origin around 7200 BP.

gray2009.citation: Gray, Drummond and Greenhill (2009). Language phylogenies reveal expansion pulses and pauses in Pacific settlement. Science 323:479–483. Approximate Taiwanese origin around 5200 years ago.

kolipakam2018.citation: Kolipakam et al. (2018). A Bayesian phylogenetic study of the Dravidian language family. Royal Society Open Science 5:171504. Approximate age 4500 years; Southworth southern-Neolithic interpretation discussed.

oracc.citation: Oracc, The Sumerian language; Digital Corpus of Cuneiform Lexical Texts. Distinguish vernacular use from later learned and scribal traditions.

glottolog.citation: Glottolog 5.3 historical time spans and representative coordinates, interpreted as broad period/location anchors.

thompson2012.citation: Thompson (2012), Bengali, introduction: early, middle and modern Bangla; language contact and learned registers.

macr1271.basis: Approximate early-modern English contact/dispersal scenario. Overseas descendants occupy destination regions; they do not define a transatlantic proto-language.

macr1273.basis: Approximate French contact/dispersal scenario. French continuity remains in northern France; later contact varieties do not relocate its ancestors.

macr1272.basis: Approximate Portuguese contact/dispersal scenario; destination populations do not imply an Atlantic ancestral homeland.

macr1270.basis: Approximate Low Countries continuity anchor, retaining Old Dutch and Middle Dutch periods and regional descendants.

glob1241.basis: Approximate Dutch contact/dispersal scenario, keeping Low Countries continuity separate from later overseas contact varieties.

paci1280.basis: Coarse nineteenth-century Pacific English-contact scenario, represented at descendant destinations rather than an oceanic centroid.

pitc1234.basis: Local contact tradition modeled from the 1790 settlement; this is not a precise date of linguistic differentiation.

nouc1234.basis: Approximate late-twentieth-century urban Ivorian contact scenario; no earlier Nouchi population is inferred from French ancestry.

cafu1238.basis: Coarse nineteenth-century Afro-Brazilian contact scenario, not a dated genetic split from Portuguese.

cast1243.basis: Approximate Iberian Castilic anchor; modern overseas coordinates do not define its homeland.

indo1319.basis: Approximate steppe-chronology homeland prior; study internal-node dates refine chronology. The coordinate is an authored regional anchor, not a measured location.

sino1245.basis: Approximate north-Chinese millet-farmer scenario; coordinate is a regional modeling anchor.

aust1307.basis: Approximate Taiwanese diversification scenario; older lineages are back-extrapolated with lower support.

drav1251.basis: Approximate southern-Neolithic scenario, not a settled homeland claim.

afro1255.basis: Weak authored northeast-African homeland and deep chronology prior; Glottolog supplies classification, not this date or homeland.

atla1278.basis: Weak authored West-African diversification prior; not the much younger Bantu expansion and not a Glottolog date.

pama1250.basis: Weak authored northern/central Australian diversification scenario; not the arrival of people or language in Australia.

aust1305.basis: Weak authored mainland Southeast Asian diversification prior.

ural1272.basis: Weak authored Ural-region diversification scenario; location and date are model assumptions.

arab1395.basis: Approximate authored late-antique Arabic diversification and expansion anchor, not a language birth date.

stan1293.basis: Approximate early-modern to modern English continuity; overseas regions expand from the captured expansion prior.

stan1290.basis: Approximate northern French continuity, including earlier related traditions rather than projecting modern standard French into the Middle Ages.

port1283.basis: Approximate western Iberian continuity; earlier Galician-Portuguese traditions are shared antecedents, not modern national boundaries.

dutc1256.basis: Approximate Low Countries continuity with overlapping historical varieties, separate from later overseas contact traditions.

oldl1238.basis: Approximate Old Latin period, extended from historical-stage metadata rather than a lexical sample.

lati1261.basis: Broad Classical-to-Late Latin continuity estimate. Regional kernels approximate Italy and later western provincial use; they do not equate Roman political borders with Latin speech.

late1252.use: late antique written and vernacular traditions
late1252.basis: Approximate, overlapping Late Latin stage, with authored regional kernels in western Roman provinces; not an exclusive territorial language.

medi1250.basis: Approximate Medieval Latin continuation around several western/central European learned centers; these authored kernels do not imply Latin was the local population's first language.

sume1241.basis: Broad Sumerian continuity model with a gradual transition to learned use around the early second millennium BCE. Southern Mesopotamian kernels approximate a region, not a precise boundary.

akka1240.basis: Broad Akkadian period and later cuneiform continuation; chronological edges are approximate.

egyp1246.use: successive Egyptian vernacular and written stages
egyp1246.basis: Broad Egyptian historical continuity estimate, modeled along the Nile valley and delta. The isolated 3000 BCE catalogue anchor is not its entire lifespan.

copt1239.basis: Approximate Coptic continuation, including later liturgical use; overlapping transition to Arabic is not an exclusive boundary.

hitt1242.basis: Broad historical Hittite period from Glottolog; distinct from the sampled vocabulary's model date.

olde1238.basis: Approximate Old English period. Authored regional kernels expand from southeastern England toward Midlands and northern centers; multilingual Britain remains overlapping, not an exclusive English territory.

midd1317.basis: Approximate Middle English period with overlapping transitions.

oldc1244.use: early Chinese inscriptional and literary traditions
oldc1244.basis: Broad Old Chinese period, with approximate Yellow River regional kernels. Neither the language's origin nor the limits of oral use are fixed by the earliest texts.

midd1344.use: historical Chinese literary and reconstructed phonological stage
midd1344.basis: Broad Middle Chinese period, not a uniform vernacular or exclusive territorial language.

sans1269.basis: Broad Sanskrit continuity model; later use is not a claim of exclusive vernacular territory.

beng1280.basis: Approximate early-to-modern Bangla continuity, retaining uncertainty and shared early eastern Indo-Aryan affiliations.

oldt1248.basis: Approximate Old Tamil historical period and transition; not a precise origin claim.

epig1241.basis: Broad Classic Maya inscriptional stage; inscriptions do not delimit all Mayan vernaculars.

stan1293.basis: Historical Old and Middle English stages associated with English continuity; an association does not equate an earlier stage with modern English.

lati1261.basis: Later Latin stages and learned continuation remain discoverable from the canonical Latin selection.

egyp1246.basis: Coptic continues the Egyptian language tradition, including its later liturgical register.

oldc1244.basis: Middle Chinese is a later historical stage associated with the earlier Chinese tradition, not the same homogeneous vernacular.

stan1288.basis: Approximate Iberian origin and overseas Spanish expansion scenario.

port1283.basis: Approximate western-Iberian origin and overseas Portuguese expansion scenario, with Brazilian growth anchored near the eastern coast rather than the modern interior.

stan1293.basis: Approximate English expansion scenario: seventeenth-century North America, eighteenth-century South Asian contact, Australian settlement from 1788, and nineteenth-century African/Pacific expansion. Regional entry points guide local growth, not exclusive borders or precise census dates. Earlier continuity uses Old and Middle English stages.

stan1290.basis: Approximate northern-French origin and overseas expansion scenario; North American growth uses an approximate Saint Lawrence entry anchor rather than a continental midpoint.

russ1263.basis: Approximate eastern-European origin and Russian expansion across northern Eurasia.

dutc1256.basis: Approximate Low-Countries origin and overseas Dutch expansion scenario.
